name: Vesicular-Apse
description: Sand owns this world, in colors from bone-white to burnt sienna, migrating with the seasons before a patient wind. Where the gusts strip it away, solar wind erosion patterns emerge like the bones of the planet.

The air carries burnt sugar and sulfur, and sound behaves strangely: footsteps crack loud, then die without echo. At night the temperature drops fast enough to hear the rock tick as it contracts. Carpet-flora blooms all at once after each rare rain, turning whole basins scarlet overnight.
Something about this world resists explanation. Every expedition answers three questions and returns with five better ones.
Survey contracts pay double for reasons nobody writes down. Veterans read the fine print, then read the survivors.
